replacements.before: Additional experiments apply the filter--quadratic--reset structure to rat cortical L5b, human cortical L2/3, hippocampal CA1, and three cerebellar cell models. Parameters are fitted separately for each cell and synaptic profile. The extension panel contains 31 inputs per operating point, with AMPA-like excitation or AMPA plus a voltage-dependent NMDA component. Appendix~\ref{app:cells} gives model accessions, cell-specific selected checkpoints, voltage errors, and event counts. These supporting experiments document voltage approximation across distinct morphologies and provide a concrete record of the event-calibration dependence across cells. The 379-input mouse comparison remains the common-dataset experiment used for the headline accuracy and timing result.
replacements.after: We also evaluate DBNN on rat cortical L5b, human cortical L2/3, hippocampal CA1, and three cerebellar cell models. DBNN is fitted separately for each cell and synaptic configuration. Each configuration is evaluated on 31 inputs, with AMPA-like excitation or AMPA plus a voltage-dependent NMDA component. Appendix~\ref{app:cells} gives model accessions, DBNN checkpoints, voltage errors, and event counts. These results show DBNN's voltage accuracy and spike prediction across different morphologies and synaptic models. The 379-input mouse panel provides the comparison of all methods on the same inputs.

replacements.before: DBNN provides a structured surrogate for repeated single-neuron simulation through site-dependent filters, a quadratic readout, and reset dynamics. replacements.after: DBNN predicts somatic voltage and spike times for repeated single-neuron simulation. Parallel filtering, fused voltage calculation, and event-based reset enable equivalent single-core CPU, multicore CPU, and GPU implementations.
